summary: Built the design as amended by the accepted findings. Rules 2 and 4 in .taad/fitness.yaml are widened in place (11 and 7 patterns), with M1 compound-operator lookaheads and M2 receiver-free Encrypt/Decrypt, and their because-texts are rewritten to claim only what a regex sees. The engine-appended SL-104 Attributes block already in the tree is kept and edited in place to the M1 pattern, with one marker only. 25 settled-only plant rows (S58-S82) are in plants.json, and the class corpus tests/bugs/SL-104-SettledRuleClassCorpus.json (178 rows, 40 census members) is judged by a new runner. The repro now exits 0 with 11 and 7 patterns read, the whole harness is 161/161 AS-RECORDED with the clean baseline CLEAN at 92 rules, and parity and RuleCases C-001..C-005 hold. The baseline build was green before any edit. I left the untracked .taad-scratch/ from the earlier stages untouched.

files.why: Rule 2 widened to 11 patterns and rule 4 to 7, because-texts rewritten, and the engine-appended SL-104 Attributes block edited in place to the M1 pattern and operator list.
25 settled-only new-file rows S58-S82 (21 designed plus S79-S82 for M1/M2), _note updated from 123 to 148 rows with a paragraph describing them.
The acceptance repro, committed exactly as the repro stage wrote it; it was untracked when the build began and is unchanged.
The corpus that closes the M1 and M2 classes: 178 fire/quiet/residual rows with a measured before column, and a 40-member census of the BCL writers and listings.

Reads the patterns from .taad/fitness.yaml, judges every corpus row and census sample, checks the Attributes entry's except_files, and checks the live .NET 10 member list against the census; -Fitness runs it against an older rules file.

obligations.how: The acceptance repro now exits 0 and prints 'All checks held.' with '11 patterns read for the timestamp rule' and '7 patterns read for the listing rule' (W01-W03 and L01-L04 fire; W20, W21, L20 and L21 stay quiet). It also passes under Windows PowerShell 5.1.
Plant row S58 (File.SetAttributes in its own file under Store/) is AS-RECORDED through the real taad3.fitness engine: xunit quiet, fitness fires rule 2, no stray hit.

Rows S59 (using static File, bare SetAttributes(...)) and S60 (bare SetLastWriteTimeUtc(...)) are AS-RECORDED; the receiver-free SetAttributes\s*\( and Set...Time(Utc)?\s*\( patterns fire rule 2 and nothing else.

S61 (new FileInfo(path).IsReadOnly = true) fires rule 2. S73 (the expression-bodied getter and IsReadOnly == true) stays quiet in both engines because of the (?![=>]) lookahead. S81 (|=) also fires. All AS-RECORDED.

S62 (ZwSetInformationFile as a call), S63 (File.Encrypt), S69 (ZwQueryDirectoryFile as a call) and S82 (FileInfo.Encrypt) each fire only their own settled rule with no stray hit, so the unproven precondition about other rules firing in Store/ is settled by measurement.

S64 (new DirectoryInfo(p).GetFiles() directly under src/FsAnalyser.Core, so ** reaches zero levels), S65 (GetDirectories with arguments in Store/) and S78 (dir.GetDirectories() in a Scanning file that is not DirectoryReader.cs) are AS-RECORDED fire rows for rule 4.
S66 (Func<FileInfo[]> list = dir.GetFiles; with no parenthesis) fires rule 4 through the \b-terminated instance pattern and is AS-RECORDED.
S67 (using static System.IO.Directory then bare GetFiles(p)) and S76 (bare EnumerateFiles(p), the composer's unmeasured widening) both fire rule 4 and are AS-RECORDED.
S68 (sealed class deriving from FileSystemEnumerator<string>) fires rule 4 through FileSystemEnumera(ble|tor) and is AS-RECORDED.

S70 (|=) and S71 (=) in Store/, S77 (&= in a Scanning file that is not excepted) and S80 (-=) all fire the new Attributes entry and are AS-RECORDED; the corpus row EX01 shows DirectoryReader.cs:181 matches the pattern and only except_files keep it quiet.

S72 (Attributes read, mask test, == comparison), S74 (File.GetAttributes, File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc) and S75 (Directory.Exists, GetFilesCount(p)) are quiet in both engines, AS-RECORDED; the corpus adds 41 more quiet rows.

harness.py --scenario clean over the unplanted tree reports xunit 18 Facts with 0 hits and fitness 92 rules, 228 files read, 0 hits, none unmatched, CLEAN. DirectoryReader.cs:181 and ShellReveal.cs's File.GetAttributes raise nothing.

rules-parity prints AGREE 18 facts <- 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns; 70 settled entries not compared (69 -> 70, twinned untouched). RuleCases -Case C-001 asserts that count as derived from the yaml, and passes under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP in 3 s; C-002..C-005 also pass.

Widened in place with no new pattern lines: time '\s*[-+]?=(?![=>])', IsReadOnly '[|&^]?=(?![=>])', Attributes entry '[-+|&^]?=(?![=>])'. The corpus enumerates the class as every property setter times every operator its type defines, plus receiver, spacing and line-break variants and the quiet comparisons, arithmetic and arrows. Against the rules as designed (M1 and M2 reverted) the corpus fails 33 checks; against 824622e it fails 90; with the fix it passes. Plant rows S79, S80 and S81 add engine-level fire rows. The because-texts name the operators.

Rule 2's Encrypt pattern is the receiver-free '(?m)\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b', still one pattern, so rule 2 holds 11. The corpus enumerates the static-versus-instance class: File and Directory statics, FileInfo and DirectoryInfo instances, method groups, using static, fully qualified names, Nt/Zw/Win32 names and object initializers, with a residual row for each spelling a text rule cannot see. S82 (new FileInfo(path).Encrypt();) is an engine-level fire row. Mutating the pattern back to \bFile\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b fails 8 corpus checks.

Ran the GetMethods() enumeration of File, Directory, FileInfo, DirectoryInfo and FileSystemInfo and pinned it as the corpus census: every Set*/set_*/Encrypt/Decrypt/listing member is fenced (with its sample line), out of family (File.SetUnixFileMode and FileSystemInfo.set_UnixFileMode, which throw PlatformNotSupportedException on Windows, verified by running them; Directory.SetCurrentDirectory), or a named residual row. The runner re-enumerates on .NET 10 and fails if a member is missing. The counts stay 11 and 7. The open-ended build instruction is gone.
obligations.not_mutable: A pinned table plus the removal of an instruction. The table is checked by the corpus runner, but no single-file replacement undoes 'the enumeration was run'.

obligations.how: Exactly one '# settled by SL-104' marker exists in .taad/fitness.yaml. The engine-appended block under it was edited in place to the M1 pattern and operator list, with the exact name, files and except_files, and no second block was written. rules-parity expects and prints exactly 70 settled entries. The runner checks the entry's except_files are exactly Kernel32.cs, DirectoryReader.cs and SynchronousIoCancel.cs.

Followed M5 as an instruction to the build. S77 and S78, the rows most exposed to the twinned Scanning rules, are in Scanning files that no twinned rule covers for these lines; the run shows xunit quiet and exactly the intended settled rule firing, with 0 stray hits, so no row needed re-keying F03-style, none was deleted, and no also or also_settled entry was needed.
obligations.not_mutable: An instruction about how to record a plant that fires a twinned rule; no such plant arose, and the harness's own STRAY-HIT and MISSED-BY-XUNIT labels are the check.

obligations.how: Split as M6 asked. The rule-count guard case is a single command, RuleCases -Case C-001, which runs in 3 s and asserts the settled count (70) derived from the yaml. C-001 passed once under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, so RuleCases is TEMP-safe and the TEMP precondition is dropped. C-002..C-005 were each run on their own (7, 7, 10 and 62 s) and pass; none is chained.
obligations.not_mutable: A change to how the guard case is split into runnable commands, not to code.

deviations: The design pinned 21 plant rows (S58-S78) and a _note count of 144; the accepted M1 and M2 findings required one fire row each, so there are 25 (S79 += on a time, S80 -= on Attributes, S81 |= on IsReadOnly, S82 FileInfo.Encrypt()), 148 rows in plants.json and 161 in the all scenario.

The design said Encrypt/Decrypt is '\bFile\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b'; per accepted M2 it is the receiver-free '\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b' (still one pattern, so 11 and 7 hold). The time, IsReadOnly and Attributes patterns carry the M1 operator classes and (?![=>]).

The design said the acceptance repro is the only new test; the CLOSE-THE-CLASS obligations O-017 and O-018 required a committed corpus, so two files were added (the corpus JSON and its runner). The repro itself is committed unchanged.

The design asked for a build-time GetMethods() enumeration treated as 'a missing pattern, not a residual'; per accepted M3 the enumeration was run once and pinned as the census in the corpus, with out-of-family members (UnixFileMode, SetCurrentDirectory) and residuals named, and the runner re-checks it on .NET 10.

The design's architecture_rules entry in design-slice-1.json still shows the pre-M1 pattern (?!=), although the finding says it is updated. I edited the engine-appended block in place instead, as accepted M4 describes. The engine's _append_rules appends only rules whose name it has not seen, so a re-run should not add a duplicate.

The design said to put the guard in one case; accepted M6 asked for it to be split. Only the C-013 key exists, so its command is RuleCases C-001 (the settled-count check), and C-002..C-005 were run separately and are listed under tests.
No known-outside-defect workaround applies: this slice fixes the project's own rules, so KnownWorkarounds and its settings are untouched.
follow_ups: The untracked .taad-scratch/ (about 95 planted Planted*.cs files, copies of fitness.yaml and probe scripts) came from the repro and investigation stages and was left in place; remove it or ignore it before the slice merges, since git status shows it as untracked.
Rules 2 and 4 and the Attributes entry still have no xUnit twin, so dotnet test stays green when they break; only the Fitness check and the harness enforce them (design filed_for_later).

Residual spellings a text rule cannot see are pinned as residual corpus rows and named in the because-texts: object initializers of Attributes and times, reflection, a delegate from a using-static method group, and Encrypt/Decrypt through using static. Closing them needs a symbol-based or AST check.
Content writes and moves that change times as a side effect (File.Write*, Move, Copy, Replace, SetAccessControl) are outside rule 2's family and remain a separate design decision.

The corpus runner's live census check fails for any new Set*/set_*/Encrypt/Decrypt/listing member on .NET 10, so it can go red on a future runtime that adds one; that red is intended, and the fix is to add the member to the census.
